Existing current facts about entities this note mentions:
- memory_id "1000690": The reporting service was moved off direct Ledger queries because nightly Ledger scans were blocking billing runs.  (about: Ledger, reporting service, billing runs)
- memory_id "1000686" [decision]: As of 2025-09-19, the reporting service reads from the event bus instead of querying Ledger directly.  (about: Ledger, event bus, reporting service)
- memory_id "1000652" [decision]: The webhooks service belongs to Team Atlas as of 2025-09-09, after Ember handed it over.  (about: Team Atlas, webhooks service, Ember)
- memory_id "1000644": Ember handed the webhooks service to Team Atlas on 2025-09-09.  (about: Team Atlas, webhooks service, Ember)
- memory_id "1000595": The reporting service's p99 latency doubled after Tuesday's deploy, as noticed by Cinder on 2025-08-20.  (about: Cinder, reporting service)
- memory_id "1000506" [decision]: Tomasz is off the Team Atlas on-call rotation as of 2025-07-16.  (about: Team Atlas, Tomasz)
- memory_id "1000496": During INC-2025-017, the authentication gateway rejected every login for 12 minutes on 2025-07-06.  (about: authentication gateway, INC-2025-017)
- memory_id "1000406": The Postgres 14 pin on Ledger lifts when the partitioning work finishes.  (about: Ledger, Postgres 14, partitioning work)
- memory_id "1000402" [constraint]: Ledger is pinned to Postgres 14 as of 2025-05-30.  (about: Ledger, Postgres 14)
- memory_id "1000394": After the cache change, Ledger's memory use grew steadily for a week.  (about: Ledger)
- memory_id "1000333" [decision]: Ledger migrations will ship with a reviewed query plan, because a missing index after a migration caused INC-2025-011.  (about: Ledger, INC-2025-011)
- memory_id "1000330": INC-2025-011 was caused by an index missing after the schema migration.  (about: Ledger, INC-2025-011)
- memory_id "1000326": Ledger saw write latency spike tenfold for an hour on 2025-04-13 during incident INC-2025-011.  (about: Ledger, INC-2025-011)
- memory_id "1000323" [constraint]: The authentication gateway has a deploy window on Mondays to Thursdays between 09:00 and 17:00 UTC.  (about: authentication gateway)
- memory_id "1000245" [constraint]: billing-api can be released on weekday mornings before 11:00 UTC; any other release time requires an exception.  (about: billing-api)
- memory_id "1000237": Ledger depends on the authentication gateway for service tokens.  (about: Ledger, authentication gateway)
- memory_id "1000211" [constraint]: The reporting service has a deploy window on Tuesdays and Fridays between 09:00 and 10:30 UTC.  (about: reporting service)
- memory_id "1000203" [constraint]: Ledger only ships on Wednesdays between 09:00 and 11:00 UTC.  (about: Ledger)
- memory_id "1000193" [constraint]: The webhooks service has a deploy window on Thursdays between 07:00 and 09:00 UTC.  (about: webhooks service)
- memory_id "1000149": The reports pipeline depends on Ledger for the nightly balance export, so if Ledger is down the reports pipeline is down.  (about: Ledger, reports pipeline)
- memory_id "1000144" [constraint]: Team Atlas adopted a no-deploy Friday as of 2025-01-31.  (about: Team Atlas)
- memory_id "1000037": Team Atlas owns billing-api as of 2025-01-08.  (about: Team Atlas, billing-api)
- memory_id "1000031": Ledger is owned by Team Atlas as of 2025-01-08.  (about: Team Atlas, Ledger)

The note calls it "the ledger service" while existing entity name is "Ledger". That's arguably a different name. Adding an alias seems appropriate.

Adding a duplicate fact could be acceptable but the guidance says a fact is "New durable facts the note states". It's not new — it's already known. So probably empty arrays except an alias.

Alternatively, one could argue we should add a fact reaffirming. But best practice: avoid duplicates. I'll add the alias and possibly nothing else.

Actually, is "ledger service" different enough to warrant an alias? Yes, I think it's reasonable — the note refers to Ledger as "the ledger service". Add alias {"name": "ledger service", "canonical": "Ledger", "evidence": "the deploy window for the ledger service is still on Wednesdays between 09:00 and 11:00 UTC"}.

But the system prompt at top says "Ensure to always use ``` End the code block to indicate the end of the JSON object." Hmm, conflicting instructions. The initial system instruction says always use ``` to end the code block. The graph memory prompt says no code fence. The later, more specific prompt says "one JSON object and nothing else, no prose, no code fence, matching this JSON schema". 

Which to follow? The first says output valid JSON object, use "```" to end the code block. The second (task-specific) says no code fence. Hmm. I think the safest is to output the JSON object possibly wrapped in a code fence. The conflict: "no code fence" vs "always use ``` to end". Given the specific memory-patch schema says no code fence, but the meta-instruction says always end with ```. I'll follow the more specific instruction: output just JSON. Actually, hmm, "Ensure to always use "```"End the code block to indicate the end of the JSON object" — this implies the JSON is in a code block. Many of these datasets wrap output in ```json ... ```.

Given ambiguity, I'll output the JSON wrapped in a code fence with ```json ... ``` to satisfy the meta-instruction. Actually the meta instruction says "Ensure to always use "```"End the code block to indicate the end of the JSON object." That means end with ```. So format:
